clinical_knowledge.topic: Chronic Insomnia Disorder evaluation and management
core_concepts: Chronic insomnia disorder requires persistent sleep difficulty despite adequate opportunity and associated daytime impairment.
Assess sleep schedule, depression, anxiety, mania, substance use, medicines, sleep apnoea, restless legs syndrome, and circadian disturbance.
CBT-I is first-line; use a sleep diary and address conditioned wakefulness and clock-watching.
Any sedative-hypnotic requires individualized risk review, short duration, and monitoring for sedation, falls, interactions, and dependence.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: difficulty falling asleep taking over 2 hours every night with daytime fatigue

Key HPI features: 46F reports 6 months of severe conditioned insomnia. Takes over 2 hours to fall asleep at night, waking up multiple times and lying awake clock-watching. Suffers from daytime fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Chronic Insomnia Disorder.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Chronic Insomnia Disorder.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Offer CBT-I including stimulus control, sleep scheduling, and cognitive strategies.
Address medical, psychiatric, and substance-related contributors.
Avoid routine long-term sedative-hypnotics and urgently assess suicidality, mania, psychosis, or unsafe impairment such as drowsy driving.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
